period_note: Year-end position from the Annual Report 2014's own 'Financial Highlights - The Premier Bank Limited & Consolidated' table, Solo column (this table gives explicit side-by-side Solo ('The Premier Bank Ltd') and Consolidated columns, unlike the same report's separate 'Performance Highlights for Five Years 2010-2014' chart section, which is Consolidated basis - confirmed since its Total Assets of 111,576.41 matches this table's Consolidated column of 111,576.40, not the Solo 110,984.04). Reserve fund is calculated as Total Equity minus Paid-up Capital (this report's Solo statutory/other reserve split was not separately extracted, so this combined figure includes retained earnings, unlike the narrower statutory+other-only definition used for FY2011-2013; consistent with this broader definition being reconcilable to reported 'Reserve and Surplus' figures in later reports' five-year tables for other years). Total liabilities is calculated as Total Assets minus Total Equity (not directly reported in this table). EPS (1.53) and NAV/share (15.89) are Solo as directly reported. Return on equity (9.64%) is reported and independently confirmed to be period-end (863.75 PAT / 8,958.17 equity = 9.64%), not average (the table's separate 'Return on average shareholders' fund' of 10.18% is the average-equity variant, not used here). Tier-1/Tier-2 capital breakdown and Total Capital in absolute Taka could not be reliably isolated for this specific year at Solo level (a Basel note figure found in this report's text did not reconcile with any other year's confirmed capital figures and was not used); CAR% alone (13.35%, Solo, directly reported) is retained. Authorized Capital, Branches, Employees and Foreign Correspondents are basis-neutral operating/company-law disclosures, taken from the FY2016 report's own five-year comparative row for FY2014 (this report's own five-year chart did not print exact figures in extractable table form for branches/employees, only bar-chart labels, which independently show the same 92/1,350).
